prompt: Are there limitatiions to a systematic review that included literature of studies made both before and after covid
judge_reasoning: Response [1] most directly answers the prompt by listing clear, review-relevant limitations when a systematic review includes studies from both before and after COVID-19 (e.g., heterogeneity, bias, comparability/generalizability). Response [4] is also strong and largely aligned, but it reframes the question more toward meta-analyses across time and is slightly less tied to “systematic review” specifics. Response [3] focuses more on challenges of integrating pre/post data at the study level rather than explicitly on systematic review methodology. Response [2] is more about the post-COVID research landscape and trends (e.g., rapid reviews, preprints) and less about the specific issue of mixing pre- and post-COVID evidence in one review.
